analysis: Documentation-only changes: docs/architecture/inference.md (head excerpts at lines 400-1097 only; the diff itself was not supplied, so I could not tell which lines changed) and docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md (patch at hunk @@ -14,6 +14,15, new paragraph on startup calibration; date bump to 2026-10-13). No code, config or control changes in the supplied units. The excerpt describes MTP idle upgrade (drain/commitIfIdle/finishDrain), typical-acceptance MTP (approximate output, sampled-output quality unqualified), MiMo native owner lifecycle and media decode memory accounting, Qwen4 admission, and coordinator-serving channels. It states there is no local HTTP endpoint and no change to consumer routing. The qualification doc says startup calibration does not qualify timing envelopes, raise concurrency or lower memory reserves. The relevant threat-model entries appear unaffected: T-041 (prefix cache and SSD), T-028, T-010, T-029 and T-008 are not weakened by the supplied text. The prefix-cache statements in inference.md (complete SSD checkpoints for MTP/Nemotron, streamed matched checkpoint with no idle payload RAM) still match T-041's posture of HMAC-keyed names, TTL and KEK-wipe purge. Residual: the diff for inference.md was not visible, so any removed or changed security-relevant claims could not be assessed. No new attack surface or invalidated assumptions found. A later pass should check that the code behind the documented behavior (ProviderLoop+MTPDrain, ModelIdleUpgrade, startup calibration) is changed elsewhere in the PR and is consistent with T-010/T-029 availability handling and T-041 cache identity.
